g_roast: In sixteen years of fourteen-year-olds, class, I never had a group that ignored the plan so politely and so completely.
There's a battle in 1410 that went better than our last fight, and in that one the general fell off his horse.
g_fire_back: That's very good, and I'll mark it as a pass. Next time, though, try to say it when I'm not holding the door for you.
My back row said worse every Tuesday, and they spelled it better, which is the part that really stings.
g_pile_on: Let me add the footnote, class. That was the second time today, and the first one was in front of a signpost.
In their defence, history is full of people who walked confidently in the wrong direction. Most of them got statues.
lines.g_peacemake: Both of you sit down, please, and drink some tea. We'll take it in order, first one side, then the other, and nobody interrupts.
lines.g_take_side: Forgive me, but I'm with this one. I've seen this argument in four centuries of textbooks, and it always ends the same way.
lines.g_left_out: You two are deep in something private, so I'll leave you to it. There's a map that wants drawing over by the fire.
lines.g_include: Come and sit with us, there's tea and there's room. Standing at the edge of the room was always the loneliest seat in class.
lines.g_bad_plan: Here's a plan from the history books. We march straight up the middle in our best clothes, and we hope they're as polite as we are.
lines.g_plan_yes: Good, that's a sensible plan. Tell me how long you need me to hold, and I'll hold exactly that long.
lines.g_plan_no: No, I'm sorry, I've read how that one ends, and there's a whole chapter on it. We'll find another way.
lines.g_hype: Right, class, the lesson's simple today. Stay behind me, watch your neighbour, and nobody wanders off.
lines.g_toast: A short toast, I promise, which from a teacher is a rare thing. To this class, who keep coming back after the bell.
lines.g_cheers: Budmo, everyone, which means let's keep being, more or less. It's a good thing to drink to.
g_quiet_line: There was a tower here once, before this one, and nobody remembers who built either. That's most of history, really.
The tea's gone cold again, and that's the third time today. Clearly I'm talking too much.
lines.g_after_wipe: Everyone up slowly, and nobody blame anybody yet. First we breathe, then we work out what happened, then we fix it.
lines.g_crew: When the bell stopped ringing for good, I thought I'd never have a class again. And here you all are, refusing to do the homework.
lines.g_exasperated: I explained it, I drew it in the dirt, I asked if there were questions. And still every one of you ran left.
lines.g_love_sharp: You ask the question under the question, the one that matters. That's the student every teacher hopes for.
lines.g_love_kind: You care for people without needing them to notice. In my experience that's the rarest lesson of all to learn.
lines.g_love_funny: You laughed at my joke about the Treaty of Andrusovo, the only person who ever has. I'll treasure that.
lines.g_love_brave: You go first when it's frightening, and you don't make a speech about it. That kind of courage is very old and very quiet.
lines.g_love_steady: You don't panic, even when the room does. A wall knows another wall, and it's good to have a second one.
lines.g_love_clever: You see the pattern before the rest of us, the way a good historian does. It's a pleasure to watch you think.
lines.g_love_honest: You tell people what's so, even the hard version. I taught the hard version every spring, so I respect that.
lines.g_love_quiet: You don't fill the silence, and you let a person think. Most people are afraid of that, and you're not.
lines.g_love_fierce: You hold on when anybody sensible would let go. History belongs to stubborn people, mostly, and you're one of them.
lines.g_love_warm: Being near you feels like the staff room on a good Friday, kettle on, everybody laughing. I'd forgotten that feeling.
g_loved: That's very kind of you, and I'm going to drink my tea and pretend I'm not moved.
Thank you, truly. Nobody's given me a good mark in a long time.
lines.g_hate_sharp: You go for the soft place every time, and you enjoy it. I've known bullies in uniform who were gentler.
lines.g_hate_kind: You keep fussing over me as if I'm fragile. I'm a large man who stands in front of things, I promise you I'll manage.
lines.g_hate_funny: Not everything is a joke, and some things deserve a moment of quiet first. You'll understand that one day, I hope.
lines.g_hate_brave: You charge in before you've looked, and somebody always has to stand in the gap you leave. Usually that's me.
lines.g_hate_steady: You wait and wait for certainty, and the moment passes. History is mostly people who waited a day too long.
lines.g_hate_clever: You explain things to people as if they're slow. A good teacher never does that, and you'd make a poor one.
lines.g_hate_honest: Truth with no care in it is just a stone you've thrown. You can be right and still be cruel.
lines.g_hate_quiet: You sit there and say nothing, and then nobody knows what you need. Silence isn't always wisdom.
lines.g_hate_fierce: Everything with you is a battle, even breakfast. I taught four wars a year, and none of them started over porridge.
lines.g_hate_warm: You talk without a pause, and nobody else can get a word in. Let the quiet ones speak, please.
lines.g_respect: We don't get on, and I won't pretend we do. But you held your ground back there, and I'll give you full marks for it.
lines.g_call_out: That one was yours, and I'll say it plainly. I asked you to wait for my signal, and you didn't wait.
lines.g_stung: I see, thank you for telling me. I'll take a short walk and think about it.
lines.g_concede: You were correct, and I was not, and I've been turning it over since. A teacher who can't say that should retire.
lines.g_nod: And well done to you too, it was good work. We'll leave it at that, before one of us gets sentimental.
lines.g_callback_save: I haven't forgotten you hauling me back to my feet. A large man is very difficult to lift, and you managed.
lines.g_callback_clutch: Just you and me left, back to back, both of us out of breath. I'll be telling that story to children one day.
lines.g_callback_callout: When you corrected me that time, I went very quiet for a day. You were right, and it was a useful lesson.
lines.g_former_rivals: At the start I had you written down as a difficult student. These days I'd put my shield between you and anything, without a second thought.
lines.g_changed: For sixteen years I taught that people don't really change, only their circumstances. Lately I'm marking my own homework wrong.
g_unguarded: Since nobody else is listening, here it is. Two of my six children at the Sepulcher stopped coming, and I've been too afraid to ask them why.
My father drove a tram in Lviv for thirty years, the number two line. Some nights I can still hear the bell, and it's a comfort.
lines.g_clipped: Yes, all right, as you like. I'll hold the road.
lines.g_noticed_open: Look at that, a whole thought, out loud, in front of everybody. Go on, please, I've been hoping you'd raise your hand.
arg_ask: {player}, would you settle this for us, please? We've both made our case, and neither of us is listening.
You decide, {player}, and we'll both abide by it. That's how it worked in my classroom, more or less.
lines.arg_backed_me: Thank you, {player}. That's what the evidence said, and I'm glad you read it too.
lines.arg_backed_them: Very well, that's your judgement, and I'll respect it. I may still write a small note in the margin.
lines.arg_stayed_out: You'd rather not choose, and that's a reasonable position. Many wise people have taken it.
lines.arg_always_their_side: Again it goes to them, {player}, every time we disagree. I've noticed, and I'd rather say so gently than stay quiet.
lines.arg_wallflower: Since nobody will decide, I'll do it the teacher's way. The evidence is on my side, and that's the end of the lesson.
lines.arg_reject: No, {player}, I can't go along with that one. I've read too many chapters that started exactly this way.
lines.arg_grumble: I still believe the evidence was with me. I won't press it, but I'll note it.
lines.arg_settled: Let's call it a shared answer, then, half marks each. That's more generous than I was with my students.
lines.seen_listens: You let a person finish their thought, {player}, which is rarer than gold. Most of my colleagues never learned it.
lines.seen_truth: You give people the true version, {player}, even when the easy one is right there. I taught the hard version too.
lines.seen_jokes: When the room goes tense you make it laugh, {player}. Teachers do that on bad days, and it's a kind of care.
lines.seen_stays_out: You keep clear of the quarrels, {player}. That's wise, though sometimes a teacher has to step in.
lines.seen_biased: One of us gets the lion's share every time, {player}. Children notice favourites first, and so do grown men.
lines.seen_harsh: You can be sharp with people, {player}. I've a thick skin from the classroom, but not everyone here has one.
lines.seed_right: Your advice after that dreadful fight, {player}, I didn't like it at all. I tried it today, and it worked, so you were right.
lines.seed_remember: I'm still thinking about what you told me when things went wrong. I haven't reached a conclusion yet, but I'm close.
lines.seed_wrong: I tried your suggestion, {player}, and it went worse, I'm afraid. I thought you'd want to know honestly.
lines.talk_aftermath_near_death: Would you sit with me a moment, {player}? That one came very close, closer than I'd like the others to see.
lines.talk_aftermath_wipe: We all went down, every one of us. Let's go through it in order, slowly, the way I'd go through a battle with a class.
lines.talk_aftermath_blame_self: {name} was the first to fall, and I was the wall. A wall has one job, {player}, and today I didn't do it.
lines.talk_aftermath_first_clear: We did it, beginning to end, and everyone walked out. If I still had a register, I'd mark today in gold.
lines.talk_development: An odd question for you, {player}. Have you noticed me changing? A student once said I'd been the same since the Middle Ages.
lines.talk_relationship_hard_on: I've been stern with {name}, too stern, I think. A teacher's voice can land like a stone if you're not careful.
lines.talk_relationship_likes_me: Give me a straight answer, {player}. Does {name} like having me around, or am I just the old man with the shield?
lines.talk_relationship_respect_hate: I find {name} very difficult, {player}. And yet if the road were breaking, they're the one I'd want beside me.
lines.talk_relationship_acting_off: {name} has gone quiet in a way I don't like, {player}. I've seen children go quiet like that, and it's rarely nothing.
lines.talk_confrontation_favour: I'd like a word, {player}, a fair one. The best equipment keeps going to {name}, and the others are watching it go.
lines.talk_confrontation_dislike: I'll be honest, because I'd rather you heard it from me. {name} and I don't get along, and I've stopped hiding it.
lines.talk_confrontation_risks: We keep taking roads we have no business on, {player}. I'll hold any line you ask, but I'd like it to be worth holding.
lines.talk_confrontation_wrong: It's {name}, {player}. Their judgement was sound and mine was not, and I'd rather say so before my pride argues back.
lines.talk_confrontation_trust: May I ask you plainly, {player}? When it matters most, you leave me behind. Is that tactics, or is it what you think of me?
lines.talk_confrontation_decided: My equipment went to {name}, and nobody spoke to me first. I'd have given it gladly, {player}, if I'd been asked.
lines.talk_lands_aftermath: Thank you, {player}, that does help. Let's have some tea.
lines.talk_shrug_aftermath: I'll be all right, in time. I usually am, slowly.
lines.talk_stings_aftermath: That wasn't what I needed to hear, I'm afraid. I'll go and stand by the road for a while.
lines.talk_lands_development: So you've seen the change too. Good, then I'm not imagining things.
lines.talk_shrug_development: Perhaps, perhaps not, the evidence is mixed. We'll see what the next chapter says.
lines.talk_stings_development: No, I don't think that's right, {player}. You've misread that page, gently.
lines.talk_lands_relationship: That's fair, thank you. I'll go and speak with {name}, carefully.
lines.talk_shrug_relationship: It may be so, or it may not. People are the hardest subject, and I taught history.
lines.talk_stings_relationship: Then we'll close the book on it, please. And I'd ask you not to repeat it to {name}.
lines.talk_lands_confrontation: That's a fair answer, and I accept it. I'm a little bruised, but it'll pass.
lines.talk_shrug_confrontation: I've heard you, {player}. Let me think about it over some tea.
lines.talk_stings_confrontation: I see, so that's the answer, then. Thank you for being clear with me.
lines.talk_door_closed: No, I'd rather not go back over this one. You'll find me holding the road if you need me.
lines.arc_cracks: One of the children asked me today what history was for, if the world's gone. I didn't have an answer, {player}, and I always have an answer.
lines.arc_turn: I used to believe you could teach people out of doing terrible things. Out here I've watched good people choose them anyway. I'm not sure what I believe now.
lines.arc_become: I still believe it, {player}, the teaching. Not because it always works, but because the one time it does is worth every time it doesn't.
lines.arc_failed: Perhaps nothing I taught ever mattered. I'll stand on the road, that's what I'm good for, and the chalk can stay in the bag.
lines.alt_turn: I've been holding this road for three years now, {player}, and some mornings I can't remember why. The wall's getting thin.
lines.alt_become: I'm only a wall now, I think. The teacher went somewhere along the road, and I didn't notice him leave.
g_roast_after: The worst class I ever taught, and I'd teach every one of you again, homework and all.
Look at you all, late, loud and lost, and I wouldn't swap a single one of you for a school.
lines.g_after_wipe_after: Everyone up, slowly, and look at me. We fell, we learn, we go again, and that's the only lesson history ever really teaches.
lines.g_toast_after: To my class, the best I ever had. You reminded an old teacher why he started.
lines.g_crew_after: This is my school now, you lot, here, wherever the road goes. It's one room, and it's enough.
g_quiet_line_after: I taught the children the four wars again today, the whole lesson. Every one of them stayed, and it was a good day.
My chalk's nearly gone, and I'm going to have to ask a dwarf for more. That feels like progress.
g_loved_after: Thank you, and I believe you. I'll carry that further than you'd guess.
That's a lovely thing to say, and I'll keep it with the tea.

history.open: I taught history to fourteen-year-olds for sixteen years, {player}. Every spring the same four wars, and every spring a new class who thought it couldn't happen to them.

options.text: And why do you think that is?
options.reply: Ha, you've stolen my line, and I'm delighted. Because it never looks like history while you're inside it. It looks like Tuesday.
Most of them, most years, a little. That's all a teacher gets, and it's more than enough.
Every day, at about nine in the morning, when the first bell would ring. Some days it's worse than others.

history.open: I have six children at the Sepulcher, {player}, twice a week. I teach them whatever I can remember of a world that isn't coming back.

options.reply: Rivers, mostly, and kings, and how ordinary people talk themselves into things. They like the kings best, naturally.
It's a ruined crypt with a draught, but thank you. On a good day it almost feels like one.

history.open: This flask was a gift from my wife, {player}, Oksana, on my first day as a teacher. She was an archivist, and she died when our son was fifteen.

options.reply: She could find anything in any archive in Lviv, and she could never find her keys. She laughed at my jokes, which proves she loved me.
Thank you, it was a long time ago. The tea still tastes better in this flask, and I'm not going to apologise for that.

friend.open: I have a son, {player}, Andriy, twenty-six now. He was studying engineering in Krakow when it happened. We argued about history at dinner every night, and I'd give anything for one more argument.

options.reply: Thank you, I'd like that very much. I check every list, and I haven't found him, but I haven't stopped.
Everything, the Cossacks mostly. He was wrong about all of it, and he was so good at being wrong.

sworn.open: I've stood in front of a great many people, {player}, children and strangers and fools. You're the first in a long while I'd choose to stand in front of. That's my whole speech.

options.reply: Then we'll hold the road together, as long as it needs holding. Have some tea.
It's the shortest I've ever given, and the only one I meant every word of.

reconciled.open: {name} and I have gone over it together, in order, from the beginning. We're at peace now, and I wanted you to know.

options.reply: Thank you, though they did most of the hard work. I mostly poured the tea.

options.text: Did you draw a map of it?
options.reply: A small one, in the dirt, yes. They thought it was very funny, and it helped.
